note.p: Thomas Sanford Gathright was born on January 5, 1829 in Monroe County, Georgia. He was the operator of Summerville Institute, a boys’ private school in Gholson County, Mississippi from 1854 to 1876. Gathright was then appointed to the superintendent of public instruction by the Mississippi Senate and Governor John Marshall Stone on April 3, 1876. He became the first president of the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas after being appointed by Jefferson Davis on October 4, 1876. In 1879, the entire administration was dismissed and Gathright served as the president of Henderson Male and Female college until his death on May 24, 1880.

scopecontent.p: This collection contains correspondence and a news release from Thomas S. Gathright, the first president of the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas (now Texas A&M University). Gathright also wrote correspondence before his presidency as the founder of the Summerville Institute in Gholson, Mississippi and during his residency as the Superintendent of Public Instruction of Mississippi. Some of the letters in the collection were transcribed in *Early History of Texas A&M College Through Letters and Papers* (1952), by David Brooks Cofer. Also included, is a folder containing xerox copies of Gathright's letters and a news release from the Mississippi State Archives.

arrangement.p: This collection is arranged chronologically by year with the folder of xerox copies at the end of the collection.
